description: EUCROPMAP is the Joint Research Centre's map of crop types in the European Union for 2018 at 10 metre resolution, described as the first continental crop type map built from Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar observations. Random forest classifiers trained on the LUCAS 2018 Copernicus in-situ survey detect 19 crop types, and accuracy was assessed with independent LUCAS core observations, with farmers' declarations covering more than 3 million parcels and 8.21 million hectares in six member states or regions, and by comparing crop areas with statistics. The data set is published in the JRC Data Catalogue with a DOI (10.2905/JRC.6ZVVSM8) and a WMS service, and the method is in d'Andrimont et al., Remote Sensing of Environment 266 (2021). Coverage is the EU. Access is free; the licence was not visible on the rendered catalogue page. Caveats: it represents one year (2018). For simulation it gives field-scale crop types for exposure of agriculture to floods, droughts and heat and for supply scenarios across Europe. Related catalogue records include Eurostat LUCAS and the USDA Cropland Data Layer.
